prayerExcerpt.en-US: The martyrs died as the outcasts of the world, but are crowned by God with immortal honor.
prayerExcerpt.pt-BR: Os mártires morreram como párias do mundo, mas são coroados por Deus com honra imortal.

meta.face: Two clearly different figures, both olive-skinned. NAZARIUS (left), a Roman of about forty-five, CLEAN-SHAVEN in the Roman manner with a dark shadow on the jaw: a TALL, RECTANGULAR face with a LONG MIDFACE — a high, straight forehead, a LONG nose with a pronounced BUMP high on the bridge, HOODED grey eyes set LOW under straight, heavy dark brows, a LONG UPPER LIP over a wide, thin-lipped mouth, a squared chin; close-cropped black hair greying at the temples; a calm, resolute gaze forward. CELSUS (right), a boy of about fourteen: a SHORT, WIDE face — a broad, low forehead under a thick, STRAIGHT black fringe cut round like a bowl, a short nose with a wide, flat bridge, big, round, dark eyes set wide under low, straight brows, full cheeks, a WIDE mouth, a small, rounded chin; looking up at Nazarius with trust. No curls on the boy.
meta.basis: No likeness survives; all that is certain is that Ambrose found their bodies in a garden outside Milan (Paulinus, Vita Ambrosii). The book makes Nazarius a Roman preacher and Celsus the youth he took with him; the faces are ours, a grown man and a boy.
